Works published in 1928, including Steamboat Willie (the earliest version of Mickey Mouse), entered the public domain.
Four people, including the perpetrator, were killed in a vehicle attack in Rochester, New York.
Harvard University president Claudine Gay announced her resignation following allegations of plagiarism and a hearing on antisemitism.
Documents containing names of associates of Jeffrey Epstein were made available to the public.
Former Proud Boys member Christopher John Worrell was sentenced to 10 years in prison for his role in the January 6 Capitol attack.
Two people were killed and six were injured in a school shooting in Perry, Iowa; the 17-year-old shooter committed suicide at the scene.
Alaska Airlines Flight 1282 suffered uncontrolled decompression after an emergency exit door on the Boeing 737 MAX 9 blew out, leading the FAA to ground all 737 Max 9s.
Audacy, the largest radio operator in the country, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection.
Nine people were arrested after clashes at the Chabad-Lubavitch World Headquarters in Brooklyn over an illegally dug tunnel.
Michigan Wolverines defeated Washington Huskies 34–13 to win the College Football Playoff National Championship.
A storm complex caused $2.7 billion in damage, bringing a winter storm to the northern US and a tornado outbreak to the Gulf Coast.
Former New Jersey governor Chris Christie suspended his 2024 presidential campaign.
Florida-based grocer Publix opened their first Kentucky store in Louisville, entering their 8th U.S. state.
New England Patriots parted ways with longtime head coach Bill Belichick.
Texas National Guard seized a park in Eagle Pass, Texas, placing barbed wire and barriers at the border.
A US-led coalition launched air strikes at Houthi militant locations in Yemen.
Detroit Lions won their first postseason game since the 1991–92 playoffs with a 24–23 win against the Los Angeles Rams.
Green Bay Packers became the first 7th seed to defeat a 2nd seed in the NFL playoffs since the format was introduced.
Vivek Ramaswamy ended his presidential campaign after securing 7.7% of the vote in the Iowa caucuses.
Congress approved a stopgap bill to extend the deadline for government funding to March 2024, avoiding a shutdown.
Alec Baldwin was indicted for involuntary manslaughter after the accidental shooting on the set of Rust that killed Halyna Hutchins.
At least 60 people were killed across the country after two weeks of winter storms.
Governor Ron DeSantis suspended his presidential campaign after a poor showing in Iowa.
A series of shootings in Joliet, Illinois killed eight and injured one.
The Supreme Court ruled against Texas for placing barbed wire at the border with Mexico.
Kenneth Smith was executed in Alabama using nitrogen hypoxia, becoming the first death row inmate to die via this method.
In E. Jean Carroll v. Donald J. Trump, the jury awarded Carroll $83.3 million after finding Trump guilty of defamation.
AWS announced plans for two large data center facilities in Mississippi, marking a $10 billion investment.
The US suspended UNRWA funds after claims that 12 staff members participated in the October 7 attacks.
An Iranian-backed militant group launched a drone attack on a US base in Jordan (Tower 22), killing three and wounding 47.
The US imposed sanctions on Israeli settlers over the violence in the West Bank.
The Oregon Supreme Court upheld Ballot Measure 113, banning ten Republican members of the Oregon Senate for refusing to attend legislative sessions.
The 66th Annual Grammy Awards were held; 'Flowers' by Miley Cyrus won Record of the Year and Midnights by Taylor Swift won Album of the Year.
The schedule for the 2026 FIFA World Cup was released; 78 games were set to be played in the US including the final.
Marianne Williamson ended her presidential campaign after losing three Democratic primaries to President Biden.
At least six members of a family died in a house fire in East Lansdowne, Pennsylvania following a shooting.
Five US Marines were found dead after their CH-53E Super Stallion helicopter crashed in the mountains outside San Diego.
Special counsel Robert K. Hur recommended no charges against President Biden in the classified documents incident.
Tucker Carlson conducted The Vladimir Putin Interview in Moscow.
Six people, including Access Bank CEO Herbert Wigwe, were killed when their helicopter crashed near Baker, California en route to Super Bowl LVIII.
Hop-A-Jet Flight 823 suffered dual engine failure and crashed while attempting to land on Interstate 75, killing the two pilots.
Kansas City Chiefs won Super Bowl LVIII against San Francisco 49ers 25–22 in overtime, becoming the first repeat champions since 2004.
A shooting on a 4 Train at Mount Eden Avenue station in New York City killed one and injured five.
Secretary of Homeland Security Alejandro Mayorkas was impeached by the House of Representatives.
Democrat Tom Suozzi won the special election for New York's 3rd congressional district, flipping the seat vacated by George Santos.
One person was killed and at least nine were injured in a mass shooting during the Kansas City Chiefs' Super Bowl parade at Union Station.
The US launched six missile-detecting satellites into orbit in response to Russian nuclear threats in outer space.
Odysseus (IM-1) lunar lander was launched at the Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
Judge Arthur Engoron ordered Trump and his companies to pay $355 million (plus interest totaling $464 million) for fraud.
Two officers and a firefighter were killed in Burnsville, Minnesota after being fired upon while responding to a domestic incident.
The 2024 Daytona 500 was held with William Byron winning.
Biden canceled $1.2 billion of student loan debts for nearly 153,000 people.
Capital One announced an agreement to acquire Discover Financial for nearly $35 billion.
The Alabama Supreme Court ruled that frozen embryos could be considered children under state law.
A ransomware attack crippled Change Healthcare's payment system, disrupting insurance claims nationwide.
AT&T suffered network outages impacting around 71,000 customers.
Intuitive Machines' Nova-C lander became the first commercial vehicle to land on the Moon.
Air Force member Aaron Bushnell committed self-immolation in front of the Embassy of Israel in DC in protest of American support for Israel.
The Smokehouse Creek Fire in the Texas panhandle burned almost 200,000 acres, resulting in a state of emergency.
Mitch McConnell announced he would step down as Senate Republican leader in January 2025.
The United States military announced plans to begin airdropping humanitarian aid into Gaza.
Caitlin Clark broke the all-time NCAA Division I college basketball career scoring record with 3,685 points.
In Trump v. Anderson, the US Supreme Court unanimously ruled that states could not keep presidential candidates off the ballot.
Jack Teixeira pleaded guilty to leaking classified Defense Department documents and was sentenced to 16 years and eight months in prison.
The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau issued a new rule capping late fees for credit cards at $8.
Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry signed a bill adding nitrogen gas and electrocution as execution methods.
Nikki Haley suspended her 2024 presidential campaign after a poor showing on Super Tuesday, leaving Trump as the presumptive Republican nominee.
President Biden delivered his third State of the Union Address.
A highway crash near Dewhurst, Wisconsin involving a van and a semi-tractor killed nine people.
A UH-72 Lakota helicopter crashed west of McAllen, Texas, killing one border patrol agent and two National Guard soldiers.
Former Honduran president Juan Orlando Hernández was found guilty in Manhattan court of conspiring with drug traffickers.
Utah adopted its new state flag, 113 years after the adoption of its former flag.
The 96th Academy Awards were held; Oppenheimer won seven awards including Best Picture.
Five people were killed during a mass stabbing and murder–suicide in Manoa, Honolulu.
The United States deployed a Marine Corps platoon to secure the US embassy in Port-au-Prince, Haiti.
A significant early spring tornado outbreak produced 34 tornadoes and caused $5.9 billion in damage across the Midwest and Northeast.
SpaceX successfully launched the Starship rocket, the most powerful rocket ever built, though it was lost during reentry.
Jo-Ann Stores filed for chapter 11 bankruptcy after accumulating over $1 billion in debt.
Richard Slayman received a kidney from a genetically engineered pig at Massachusetts General Hospital.
The Francis Scott Key Bridge in Baltimore partially collapsed after the cargo ship MV Dali collided with it; six were presumed dead.
Four people were killed and seven were injured during a mass stabbing in Rockford, Illinois.
Sam Bankman-Fried was sentenced to 25 years in prison for wire fraud and money laundering related to FTX.
Millions of AT&T customers were affected by a data breach that leaked onto the dark web.
The Supreme Court of Florida ruled that the Florida Constitution did not confer a right to abortion, allowing the 15-week ban to remain.
A significant tornado outbreak and derecho produced 86 tornadoes and caused $1.8 billion in damage across the Midwest and Southeast.
General Electric split into three independent companies: GE Aerospace, GE Vernova, and GE HealthCare.
Bird flu spread to cattle herds in at least six US states; a dairy farm worker in Texas became the second person ever infected in the US.
A magnitude 4.8 earthquake struck New Jersey, causing tremors throughout the East Coast.
